hook.text: For 300 years, European nations believed wealth was a fixed pie. Your gain was someone else's loss.

buildup.text: Mercantilism demanded that countries export more than they import, hoarding gold and silver.

discovery.text: Governments imposed tariffs, banned certain imports, and granted monopolies to favored companies.

twist.text: Adam Smith argued in 1776 that trade creates wealth—it's not zero-sum. Free trade benefits both sides.

climax.text: Smith's ideas toppled mercantilism and birthed modern economics. Trade became about growth, not hoarding.

punchline.text: Wealth isn't a pie. Trade can grow the whole bakery.

quiz.question: Who argued against mercantilism in 'The Wealth of Nations'?

details.summary: Mercantilism was the dominant European economic doctrine from the 16th to 18th centuries, holding that national wealth came from accumulating gold and silver through trade surpluses..
details.whyItMatters: Mercantilism shaped global trade patterns for 300 years, establishing colonial empires and trade monopolies whose economic effects persist today..
takeaways: Nations competed to accumulate gold through export surpluses and import restrictions
Colonies served as captive markets and raw material sources for imperial powers
Mercantilism motivated European colonialism and monopoly trade companies

faq.question: What were the core principles of mercantilism?
faq.answer: National wealth was measured by gold and silver reserves. Exports should exceed imports to generate trade surpluses. Colonies should provide raw materials and consume manufactured goods. Government should actively manage trade through tariffs, subsidies, and monopoly grants.

faq.question: Why was mercantilism eventually replaced by free trade theory?
faq.answer: Adam Smith in The Wealth of Nations argued that trade benefits both parties, not just the exporter. David Ricardo proved comparative advantage made free trade efficient. The Industrial Revolution showed that production capacity mattered more than gold reserves for national wealth.
